name: checkout-flow-decisions
observations: Checkout is a single page; guest checkout stays enabled.
The checkout is one page with three collapsible steps. Guest checkout stays enabled because 62 % of orders in the test month came from guests.
**Why:** the two-page variant lost more carts in the A/B test.
**How to apply:** do not propose multi-page flows. Payment settings are in [[payment-provider-sandbox]].
source: projects/acme-shop/.claude/memory/checkout-flow-decisions.md

name: owner-prefers-short-answers
observations: The shop owner wants short answers and decisions with one recommendation.
Answers should be short. When there is a choice, give one recommendation and the reason in a sentence.
source: projects/acme-shop/.claude/memory/owner-prefers-short-answers.md

name: payment-provider-sandbox
observations: Sandbox dashboard and test cards of the payment provider.
Test payments run against the provider's sandbox. The published test card `4242 4242 4242 4242` works with any future expiry date.
Webhooks for the sandbox point to the staging site, see [[staging-before-live]].
source: projects/acme-shop/.claude/memory/payment-provider-sandbox.md

name: product-images-webp
observations: Product images are WebP at 1200 px, no PNG uploads.
Upload product images as WebP with a width of 1200 px and quality 82.
**Why:** PNG uploads made category pages three times heavier.
**How to apply:** convert before upload, keep the original in the shared drive.
source: projects/acme-shop/.claude/memory/product-images-webp.md

name: staging-before-live
observations: Every change goes to staging first, live only after a manual check.
Deploy to staging, test the checkout once by hand, then deploy to live.
**Why:** a template change once broke the cart button on live for two hours.
**How to apply:** never run the live deploy script without a staging run on the same day.
source: projects/acme-shop/.claude/memory/staging-before-live.md

name: newsletter-double-opt-in
observations: New subscribers always confirm by e-mail before the first send.
Double opt-in is mandatory. Imported lists are not added without confirmation.
**Why:** an imported list once caused a wave of spam complaints.
**How to apply:** refuse list imports, point to the sign-up form. Send times are in [[newsletter-send-window]].
source: projects/acme-shop/apps/newsletter/.claude/memory/newsletter-double-opt-in.md

name: newsletter-send-window
observations: Newsletters go out on Tuesdays at 10:00, never on Mondays.
The newsletter is sent on Tuesdays at 10:00 local time. Mondays had the lowest open rate in the last twelve sends.
Product images in the newsletter follow [[product-images-webp]].
source: projects/acme-shop/apps/newsletter/.claude/memory/newsletter-send-window.md

name: article-structure
observations: Articles start with the answer, then the steps, then background.
Each article opens with the answer in two sentences, followed by numbered steps and only then the background.
**Why:** readers arrive from search with one concrete question.
**How to apply:** move history and anecdotes below the steps. Plant names follow [[plant-names-latin-and-common]].
source: projects/garden-blog/.claude/memory/article-structure.md

name: plant-names-latin-and-common
observations: First mention of a plant gives the common and the Latin name.
Write the common name first and the Latin name in brackets at the first mention, for example Lavender (*Lavandula angustifolia*).
**Why:** common names differ between regions.
**How to apply:** after the first mention use the common name only.
source: projects/garden-blog/.claude/memory/plant-names-latin-and-common.md

name: seed-calendar-data
observations: The sowing calendar is a spreadsheet in the content folder, one row per plant.
The sowing calendar lives in `content/data/seed-calendar.xlsx`. One row per plant, months as columns.
Articles that mention sowing times take them from this file, see [[article-structure]].
source: projects/garden-blog/.claude/memory/seed-calendar-data.md

name: spring-series-plan
observations: Six articles on spring sowing, one per week from March.
The spring series has six articles, published weekly from the first week of March. Four are published, two are drafts.
Dates come from [[seed-calendar-data]], the layout from [[article-structure]]. Hosting notes are in [[backup-rotation]].
source: projects/garden-blog/.claude/memory/spring-series-plan.md

name: backup-rotation
observations: Nightly backups, seven daily and four weekly copies on the second disk.
Backups run nightly at 02:30. Seven daily and four weekly copies are kept on the second disk, older ones are deleted.
A restore test is due on the first Sunday of each month, see [[restore-test-checklist]].
source: projects/home-server/.claude/memory/backup-rotation.md

name: no-updates-on-fridays
observations: System updates only from Monday to Thursday.
Install system updates from Monday to Thursday only.
**Why:** a Friday kernel update left the server down over a weekend.
**How to apply:** if an update is pending on a Friday, note it and do it on Monday. Check [[backup-rotation]] ran before updating.
source: projects/home-server/.claude/memory/no-updates-on-fridays.md

name: restore-test-checklist
observations: Steps for the monthly restore test on the spare machine.
Restore the latest weekly copy to the spare machine, start the services, open the blog and the shop staging site, compare the newest article and the newest order.
Backups are described in [[backup-rotation]].
source: projects/home-server/.claude/memory/restore-test-checklist.md
